table.name: Downshift Ramp Step
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE RAMP STEP, one entry per downshift in the order 2-1, 3-1, 3-2, 4-1, 4-2, 4-3, 5-1, 5-2, 5-3, 5-4.
Once the hold period expires, the commanded pressure moves from where it started toward the target by this much. A large value - 32767 appears in the stock calibration for most entries - means effectively no limit, so the pressure goes straight to target. A small value makes the application gradual, which is what the factory calls smooth control.
This is the knob for downshift harshness. Smaller steps are softer and slower.

table.name: Downshift Ramp Hold
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE HOLD DURATION, one entry per downshift in the order 2-1, 3-1, 3-2, 4-1, 4-2, 4-3, 5-1, 5-2, 5-3, 5-4.
How long the pressure is held at its floor before the ramp starts. The value is a count of controller loops. The loop period has NOT been established, so this is left as a raw count rather than converted to milliseconds - a time unit derived from a guessed task rate would look authoritative and be wrong.
Larger values delay the pressure rise, which softens the initial engagement.

table.name: Line Pressure Target 1 - Nm
table.description:
LINE PRESSURE TARGET. Engine torque in, commanded line pressure out. This is what the pressure control solenoid is driven to achieve.
The torque axis is the engine torque the ECU reports on CAN 0x412, after the TCU has multiplied it by the Torque Converter Slip Pressure Factor, smoothed it, and multiplied it again by the ATF temperature factor. So the axis is effective torque, not raw crank torque.
Both units are confirmed against outside sources rather than inferred. The torque axis comes from the community CAN decoding of 0x412 bytes 3-4. The pressure axis reproduces the two figures in the factory manual's line pressure test: about 524 kPa at low torque against a specified 490 nominal (385-555 band), and 1372 kPa at 400 Nm against a specified 1370 at full throttle in D.
RAISING THESE RAISES CLAMPING FORCE. Firmer, faster shifts and more clutch holding capacity, at the cost of harsher engagement, more pump load and more heat. Several maps exist and the TCU selects between them by operating state - which state picks which map has NOT been established, so change them as a set unless you have logged which one is active.
This table holds ONE of the two quantities in the record array, so it can be shown in real units. Rows are the polyline vertices in order: 1a is the start of segment 1, 1b its end, 2a the start of segment 2, and so on. A segment's end normally equals the next segment's start; where it does not, the curve steps vertically at that point, which is deliberate. The companion table in the same category holds the other quantity, row for row.

The torque axis is the engine torque the ECU reports on CAN 0x412, after the TCU has multiplied it by the Torque Converter Slip Pressure Factor, smoothed it, and multiplied it again by the ATF temperature factor. So the axis is effective torque, not raw crank torque.
Both units are confirmed against outside sources rather than inferred. The torque axis comes from the community CAN decoding of 0x412 bytes 3-4. The pressure axis reproduces the two figures in the factory manual's line pressure test: about 524 kPa at low torque against a specified 490 nominal (385-555 band), and 1372 kPa at 400 Nm against a specified 1370 at full throttle in D.
RAISING THESE RAISES CLAMPING FORCE. Firmer, faster shifts and more clutch holding capacity, at the cost of harsher engagement, more pump load and more heat. Several maps exist and the TCU selects between them by operating state - which state picks which map has NOT been established, so change them as a set unless you have logged which one is active.
This table holds ONE of the two quantities in the record array, so it can be shown in real units. Rows are the polyline vertices in order: 1a is the start of segment 1, 1b its end, 2a the start of segment 2, and so on. A segment's end normally equals the next segment's start; where it does not, the curve steps vertically at that point, which is deliberate. The companion table in the same category holds the other quantity, row for row.

table.name: P0705
table.description:
P0705 - enable or disable this diagnostic trouble code.
DISABLED writes zero to this code's slot, which makes it identical to the 43 slots the factory already leaves empty. The fault bit still sets internally, but no code number is attached to it, so nothing is reported.
Know what that does and does not do. It suppresses the CODE, not the FAULT - whatever limp-home, pressure or shift behaviour the TCU applies when that bit sets will still happen. You have only stopped it telling you why. Useful after a hardware change that leaves a sensor permanently faulted; a poor idea as a way of silencing a fault you have not diagnosed.
This behaviour is inferred from the table layout, not tested on a vehicle. Zero is what the firmware's own unused slots contain, which is the best evidence available, but nobody has confirmed how a scan tool reports it.
Stored at 0x01D78C as 0x0705. The code is the P-number in hex, so this reads as P0705.

table.name: Line Pressure Target 1 (1370 kPa) - RPM
table.description:
Line pressure target against engine speed. Both columns are in real units and neither is inferred: the breakpoint column uses the same /8 engine-speed scaling confirmed elsewhere in this definition, and the value column is already in kPa.
The kPa unit is confirmed against the factory service manual line pressure test (5AT-35), which has the TCU reporting 'P/L Solenoid Target Pressure' to the Subaru Select Monitor in kPa and specifies 1370 kPa at full throttle in D and R. That value appears verbatim in this table in all eleven firmwares, at an address that relocates between them - so it is calibration data, not a coincidence.
WHAT IS NOT CONFIRMED: which hydraulic circuit each of the two curves governs. The value is flat across engine speed within each curve (1370 kPa in one, 953 kPa in the other), and the consuming function has not been traced. The tables are named for what they demonstrably contain rather than for a circuit that would be a guess.
The final breakpoint is 8160 RPM (65280 raw), a max sentinel rather than a real operating point. Raising line pressure increases clamping force and shift firmness; it also increases pump load and wear.
RPM RANGE: engine speed is a uint16 scaled by 1/8, so the highest value these tables can hold is 8191 RPM. The stock calibration already uses breakpoints as high as 8160 RPM elsewhere, so there is room to raise shift and slip breakpoints for a built engine - but a target above 8191 RPM cannot be represented here, and entering one will clip.

The kPa unit is confirmed against the factory service manual line pressure test (5AT-35), which has the TCU reporting 'P/L Solenoid Target Pressure' to the Subaru Select Monitor in kPa and specifies 1370 kPa at full throttle in D and R. That value appears verbatim in this table in all eleven firmwares, at an address that relocates between them - so it is calibration data, not a coincidence.
WHAT IS NOT CONFIRMED: which hydraulic circuit each of the two curves governs. The value is flat across engine speed within each curve (1370 kPa in one, 953 kPa in the other), and the consuming function has not been traced. The tables are named for what they demonstrably contain rather than for a circuit that would be a guess.
The final breakpoint is 8160 RPM (65280 raw), a max sentinel rather than a real operating point. Raising line pressure increases clamping force and shift firmness; it also increases pump load and wear.
RPM RANGE: engine speed is a uint16 scaled by 1/8, so the highest value these tables can hold is 8191 RPM. The stock calibration already uses breakpoints as high as 8160 RPM elsewhere, so there is room to raise shift and slip breakpoints for a built engine - but a target above 8191 RPM cannot be represented here, and entering one will clip.

table.name: Read This First
table.description:
Firmware: ABD1207000 (cal ID MB5300, JDM, 384kb)
Subaru 5EAT TCU (5-speed automatic transmission control unit), Mitsubishi/Renesas M32R CPU.
Firmware: 91D1206000 (MB431M / R9H)
Origin: JDM TCU, MCU wa12212953www (M32R, 144-pin, 384KB). Most likely a 2003-2004 JDM Legacy — the market is stated by the person who dumped it, but the exact year/model is NOT confirmed (the unit had no housing or part-number label). Note this is NOT the 05-06 USDM TCU, which uses a different MCU.
Confirmed: table addresses, DTC list, checksum, gear ratios (raw/1024), Confirmed conversions: gear ratios (raw/1024), engine speed (raw/8), temperature (raw-40 degC), vehicle speed (km/h), accelerator pedal angle (raw/255 = 0-100%). Anything left as "raw" has no confirmed conversion. Pressure units are NOT confirmed and are not stored in the ROM. See docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md for detail.
REQUIRES RomRaider 1.0.0 or later. The shift schedule and record curves are 3D tables; RomRaider 0.8.2 reports "There was an error loading table" for them.
This is a static file editor only — cannot connect live to the vehicle through RomRaider. Run tools/checksum.py after any edit, before flashing.

table.name: Shift Schedule Group Selector
table.description:
SHIFT SCHEDULE GROUP SELECTOR. The transmission carries ten complete shift schedules in each of five groups, and this table decides which GROUP is in use.
Each cell holds a selector code, not a number to scale: 0x81, 0x82, 0x83, 0x85 select schedule groups 2, 3, 4 and 1 0x80, 0x84, 0x8C select group 0 0xFF no override - the current position stands 0x00 entry unused
The firmware reads it as base + index*4 + a sub-index of -3 to +4, so the rows and columns here are the raw storage rather than two named axes; what indexes it is not established.
Worth knowing before changing anything: three firmwares - ACD1207000, ACD1A06000 and ADE0236000 - carry 0x83 where the other thirteen carry 0xFF. Those images force a gear limit where the rest leave the selector alone, so this table really does differ between calibrations and is not boilerplate.
Codes confirmed from the firmware's own comparison chain, which tests exactly 0x80 to 0x85 and 0x8C.

table.name: ATF Blend Window
table.description:
ATF TEMPERATURE BLEND WINDOW. Below the first temperature the transmission uses its cold calibration for solenoid target pressure; above the second it uses the warm one; between them it interpolates linearly between the two.
This is not per-gear or per-solenoid - all seven solenoid channels read the same pair, so widening or narrowing the window changes when every clutch and brake hands over from cold to warm behaviour.
Stock is 15 C to 135 C in every firmware examined. Raising the lower figure keeps cold-ATF pressures in use for longer; lowering the upper figure reaches full warm behaviour sooner.
Confirmed by following all seven solenoid drivers in the decompiled firmware, which interpolate on exactly these two bytes against the ATF reading.

CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve (CAN 0x511 byte 4 (from VDC/ABS), raw x1.301)

table.description: X-input is CAN ID 0x511 payload byte 4, scaled by a fixed 333/256 (~x1.301) factor before this lookup. Stock data is flat (0) — real, editable, currently inert.

table.name: Gear 1 Shift Correction
table.description:
Gear 1 of 5. Signed correction curve against engine speed, selected by a gear-indexed pointer array at 0x117A0. Gear 1 is all zeros (no correction), and the magnitude falls with each higher gear (about -1970 at the top of gear 2 down to -390 in gear 5) — the shape of a shift-shock or torque-phase correction.
Values are genuinely NEGATIVE and stored as signed 16-bit. Real-world units are not confirmed.
This family was only found after correcting the Ghidra M32R processor definition: the pointer array that selects it was unreadable before.

table.name: CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve
CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve (Reference signal breakpoint (raw, pre-scale CAN 0x410 chain value))

table.description: X-input confirmed via decompilation: the same ceiling-clamped CAN ID 0x410-derived reference value already traced in docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md (before its x256 scale-up), NOT gear-indexed — a single standalone curve. Stock data is a genuine hump shape: rises from 61 to a peak of 127 around the middle of the axis, then falls back to 0 at the high end — a real, currently-populated tunable curve.

table.name: Signal FE Response Curve
Signal FE Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, source not fully traced))

table.description: X-input is an internal RAM value (traced back through several conditional assignments in the decompiled code, but not yet to a specific sensor or CAN ID — see docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Stock data is a real, populated step curve (64 up to 256), not flat/placeholder.

table.name: Smoothed Signal Response Curve
Smoothed Signal Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, x256 of a 0-255 byte))

table.description: X-input is the same internal signal as the 'Signal FE Response Curve' table, but smoothed through a calibratable first-order filter before this lookup (confirmed via decompilation: the filter target is that byte shifted left 8, i.e. x256). This is a DIFFERENT signal chain from the engine-speed tables, so the RPM scale used on those does NOT apply here — left raw deliberately. Stock data is a real, populated rising curve (200 up to 1189).

table.name: Shift Map - ATFTempLow, 1
table.description:
THE SHIFT MAP. All eight shift points in one table, in the form a five-speed automatic is normally calibrated: vehicle speed against accelerator pedal angle, one row per shift event.
Read a cell as: this shift happens at this road speed when the pedal is at this position. Raise a value to delay the shift, lower it to bring the shift on earlier. The upshift rows come first, then the downshifts - the gap between an upshift and its matching downshift is the hysteresis that stops the transmission hunting between two gears, so move the pair together unless you specifically intend to change it.
Every value is vehicle speed in km/h, confirmed against the factory shift chart. The axis is accelerator opening angle, stored as 0-255 for 0-100%.
Cells showing '-' are not editable. They are pedal positions where that particular curve has no vertex in the ROM, so there is no byte to change. Each curve is stored as its own polyline with its own breakpoints; this table lines them up on the shared pedal axis and leaves a gap where a curve does not use a position, rather than inventing a value.
Requires the patched RomRaider in romraider-5eat/. The eight curves sit at eight separate addresses with different lengths, which upstream cannot express as one table - see Table3D.cellIndices.
The schedule used in ATFTempLow drive mode with the lever in Manual 1.
The firmware picks a schedule by index:
drive mode x 50 + shift lever x 10 + gear x 2
Drive modes are Normal, Sport#, Slope, Manual, Kickdown, ATF Temp Low, I-Mode and three not yet identified. Lever positions are D and Manual 5 together, then Manual 4, 3, 2 and 1.
Schedules share curves - a table used in D is often the same object used in Manual 5 - so editing one map can change another. Check the addresses if that matters.
The formula, the drive mode mapping and this naming are rimwall's, from the RomRaider forum thread; FINDINGS section 51 verifies them against the code.

table.name: Shift Map - IMode, 2
table.description:
THE SHIFT MAP. All eight shift points in one table, in the form a five-speed automatic is normally calibrated: vehicle speed against accelerator pedal angle, one row per shift event.
Read a cell as: this shift happens at this road speed when the pedal is at this position. Raise a value to delay the shift, lower it to bring the shift on earlier. The upshift rows come first, then the downshifts - the gap between an upshift and its matching downshift is the hysteresis that stops the transmission hunting between two gears, so move the pair together unless you specifically intend to change it.
Every value is vehicle speed in km/h, confirmed against the factory shift chart. The axis is accelerator opening angle, stored as 0-255 for 0-100%.
Cells showing '-' are not editable. They are pedal positions where that particular curve has no vertex in the ROM, so there is no byte to change. Each curve is stored as its own polyline with its own breakpoints; this table lines them up on the shared pedal axis and leaves a gap where a curve does not use a position, rather than inventing a value.
Requires the patched RomRaider in romraider-5eat/. The eight curves sit at eight separate addresses with different lengths, which upstream cannot express as one table - see Table3D.cellIndices.

table.name: Shift Map - Manual, D5
table.description:
THE SHIFT MAP. All eight shift points in one table, in the form a five-speed automatic is normally calibrated: vehicle speed against accelerator pedal angle, one row per shift event.
Read a cell as: this shift happens at this road speed when the pedal is at this position. Raise a value to delay the shift, lower it to bring the shift on earlier. The upshift rows come first, then the downshifts - the gap between an upshift and its matching downshift is the hysteresis that stops the transmission hunting between two gears, so move the pair together unless you specifically intend to change it.
Every value is vehicle speed in km/h, confirmed against the factory shift chart. The axis is accelerator opening angle, stored as 0-255 for 0-100%.
Cells showing '-' are not editable. They are pedal positions where that particular curve has no vertex in the ROM, so there is no byte to change. Each curve is stored as its own polyline with its own breakpoints; this table lines them up on the shared pedal axis and leaves a gap where a curve does not use a position, rather than inventing a value.
Requires the patched RomRaider in romraider-5eat/. The eight curves sit at eight separate addresses with different lengths, which upstream cannot express as one table - see Table3D.cellIndices.

table.name: Downshift 2-1 Pressure - km/h
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE TARGET, 2-1. The pressure commanded during this particular downshift, against vehicle speed.
Pressure is in kPa on the scale confirmed against the factory manual - these maps reach 1372 kPa, which is the manual's figure for full throttle in D.
Raising a value makes this downshift firmer and faster; lowering it makes it softer and slower, at the cost of more clutch slip during the change. Pair it with the ramp step and duration tables in this category, which control how quickly the pressure is allowed to get there.
This table holds ONE of the two quantities in the record array, so it can be shown in real units. Rows are the polyline vertices in order: 1a is the start of segment 1, 1b its end, 2a the start of segment 2, and so on. A segment's end normally equals the next segment's start; where it does not, the curve steps vertically at that point, which is deliberate. The companion table in the same category holds the other quantity, row for row.

table.name: Downshift 5-1 Pressure - km/h
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE TARGET, 5-1. The pressure commanded during this particular downshift, against vehicle speed.
Pressure is in kPa on the scale confirmed against the factory manual - these maps reach 1372 kPa, which is the manual's figure for full throttle in D.
Raising a value makes this downshift firmer and faster; lowering it makes it softer and slower, at the cost of more clutch slip during the change. Pair it with the ramp step and duration tables in this category, which control how quickly the pressure is allowed to get there.

table.name: Downshift Ramp Step
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE RAMP STEP, one entry per downshift in the order 2-1, 3-1, 3-2, 4-1, 4-2, 4-3, 5-1, 5-2, 5-3, 5-4.
Once the hold period expires, the commanded pressure moves from where it started toward the target by this much. A large value - 32767 appears in the stock calibration for most entries - means effectively no limit, so the pressure goes straight to target. A small value makes the application gradual, which is what the factory calls smooth control.
This is the knob for downshift harshness. Smaller steps are softer and slower.

table.name: Downshift Ramp Hold
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE HOLD DURATION, one entry per downshift in the order 2-1, 3-1, 3-2, 4-1, 4-2, 4-3, 5-1, 5-2, 5-3, 5-4.
How long the pressure is held at its floor before the ramp starts. The value is a count of controller loops. The loop period has NOT been established, so this is left as a raw count rather than converted to milliseconds - a time unit derived from a guessed task rate would look authoritative and be wrong.
Larger values delay the pressure rise, which softens the initial engagement.

table.name: Line Pressure Target 1 - Nm
table.description:
LINE PRESSURE TARGET. Engine torque in, commanded line pressure out. This is what the pressure control solenoid is driven to achieve.
The torque axis is the engine torque the ECU reports on CAN 0x412, after the TCU has multiplied it by the Torque Converter Slip Pressure Factor, smoothed it, and multiplied it again by the ATF temperature factor. So the axis is effective torque, not raw crank torque.
Both units are confirmed against outside sources rather than inferred. The torque axis comes from the community CAN decoding of 0x412 bytes 3-4. The pressure axis reproduces the two figures in the factory manual's line pressure test: about 524 kPa at low torque against a specified 490 nominal (385-555 band), and 1372 kPa at 400 Nm against a specified 1370 at full throttle in D.
RAISING THESE RAISES CLAMPING FORCE. Firmer, faster shifts and more clutch holding capacity, at the cost of harsher engagement, more pump load and more heat. Several maps exist and the TCU selects between them by operating state - which state picks which map has NOT been established, so change them as a set unless you have logged which one is active.
This table holds ONE of the two quantities in the record array, so it can be shown in real units. A segment's end normally equals the next segment's start; where it does not, the curve steps vertically at that point, which is deliberate. The pressure axis reproduces the two figures in the factory manual's line pressure test: about 524 kPa at low torque against a specified 490 nominal (385-555 band), and 1372 kPa at 400 Nm against a specified 1370 at full throttle in D.
RAISING THESE RAISES CLAMPING FORCE. Firmer, faster shifts and more clutch holding capacity, at the cost of harsher engagement, more pump load and more heat. Several maps exist and the TCU selects between them by operating state - which state picks which map has NOT been established, so change them as a set unless you have logged which one is active.
This table holds ONE of the two quantities in the record array, so it can be shown in real units. Rows are the polyline vertices in order: 1a is the start of segment 1, 1b its end, 2a the start of segment 2, and so on. A segment's end normally equals the next segment's start; where it does not, the curve steps vertically at that point, which is deliberate. The companion table in the same category holds the other quantity, row for row.

table.name: P0705
table.description:
P0705 - enable or disable this diagnostic trouble code.
DISABLED writes zero to this code's slot, which makes it identical to the 43 slots the factory already leaves empty. The fault bit still sets internally, but no code number is attached to it, so nothing is reported.
Know what that does and does not do. It suppresses the CODE, not the FAULT - whatever limp-home, pressure or shift behaviour the TCU applies when that bit sets will still happen. You have only stopped it telling you why. Useful after a hardware change that leaves a sensor permanently faulted; a poor idea as a way of silencing a fault you have not diagnosed.
This behaviour is inferred from the table layout, not tested on a vehicle. Zero is what the firmware's own unused slots contain, which is the best evidence available, but nobody has confirmed how a scan tool reports it.
Stored at 0x01DCC4 as 0x0705. The code is the P-number in hex, so this reads as P0705.

table.name: Line Pressure Target 1 (1370 kPa) - RPM
table.description:
Line pressure target against engine speed. Both columns are in real units and neither is inferred: the breakpoint column uses the same /8 engine-speed scaling confirmed elsewhere in this definition, and the value column is already in kPa.
The kPa unit is confirmed against the factory service manual line pressure test (5AT-35), which has the TCU reporting 'P/L Solenoid Target Pressure' to the Subaru Select Monitor in kPa and specifies 1370 kPa at full throttle in D and R. That value appears verbatim in this table in all eleven firmwares, at an address that relocates between them - so it is calibration data, not a coincidence.
WHAT IS NOT CONFIRMED: which hydraulic circuit each of the two curves governs. The value is flat across engine speed within each curve (1370 kPa in one, 953 kPa in the other), and the consuming function has not been traced. The tables are named for what they demonstrably contain rather than for a circuit that would be a guess.
The final breakpoint is 8160 RPM (65280 raw), a max sentinel rather than a real operating point. Raising line pressure increases clamping force and shift firmness; it also increases pump load and wear.
RPM RANGE: engine speed is a uint16 scaled by 1/8, so the highest value these tables can hold is 8191 RPM. The stock calibration already uses breakpoints as high as 8160 RPM elsewhere, so there is room to raise shift and slip breakpoints for a built engine - but a target above 8191 RPM cannot be represented here, and entering one will clip.

table.name: Read This First
table.description:
Firmware: ACD1207000 (cal ID MB558D01, JDM, 512kb)
Subaru 5EAT TCU (5-speed automatic transmission control unit), Mitsubishi/Renesas M32R CPU.
Firmware: 91D1206000 (MB431M / R9H)
Origin: JDM TCU, MCU wa12212953www (M32R, 144-pin, 384KB). Most likely a 2003-2004 JDM Legacy — the market is stated by the person who dumped it, but the exact year/model is NOT confirmed (the unit had no housing or part-number label). Note this is NOT the 05-06 USDM TCU, which uses a different MCU.
Confirmed: table addresses, DTC list, checksum, gear ratios (raw/1024), Confirmed conversions: gear ratios (raw/1024), engine speed (raw/8), temperature (raw-40 degC), vehicle speed (km/h), accelerator pedal angle (raw/255 = 0-100%). Anything left as "raw" has no confirmed conversion. Pressure units are NOT confirmed and are not stored in the ROM. See docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md for detail.
REQUIRES RomRaider 1.0.0 or later. The shift schedule and record curves are 3D tables; RomRaider 0.8.2 reports "There was an error loading table" for them.
This is a static file editor only — cannot connect live to the vehicle through RomRaider. Run tools/checksum.py after any edit, before flashing.

table.name: Shift Schedule Group Selector
table.description:
SHIFT SCHEDULE GROUP SELECTOR. The transmission carries ten complete shift schedules in each of five groups, and this table decides which GROUP is in use.
Each cell holds a selector code, not a number to scale: 0x81, 0x82, 0x83, 0x85 select schedule groups 2, 3, 4 and 1 0x80, 0x84, 0x8C select group 0 0xFF no override - the current position stands 0x00 entry unused
The firmware reads it as base + index*4 + a sub-index of -3 to +4, so the rows and columns here are the raw storage rather than two named axes; what indexes it is not established.
Worth knowing before changing anything: three firmwares - ACD1207000, ACD1A06000 and ADE0236000 - carry 0x83 where the other thirteen carry 0xFF. Those images force a gear limit where the rest leave the selector alone, so this table really does differ between calibrations and is not boilerplate.
Codes confirmed from the firmware's own comparison chain, which tests exactly 0x80 to 0x85 and 0x8C.

table.name: ATF Blend Window
table.description:
ATF TEMPERATURE BLEND WINDOW. Below the first temperature the transmission uses its cold calibration for solenoid target pressure; above the second it uses the warm one; between them it interpolates linearly between the two.
This is not per-gear or per-solenoid - all seven solenoid channels read the same pair, so widening or narrowing the window changes when every clutch and brake hands over from cold to warm behaviour.
Stock is 15 C to 135 C in every firmware examined. Raising the lower figure keeps cold-ATF pressures in use for longer; lowering the upper figure reaches full warm behaviour sooner.
Confirmed by following all seven solenoid drivers in the decompiled firmware, which interpolate on exactly these two bytes against the ATF reading.

table.name: Gear 1 Slip Comp Pressure B
Gear 1 Slip Comp Pressure B (Accelerator pedal angle x256 minus reference speed (raw))

table.description: Gear 1 of 5. Pressure/duty correction curve. The X-input is (accelerator pedal angle x 256) minus the Reference Speed Baseline lookup — a difference, so the axis itself is raw even though both operands are now identified. Pedal angle arrives on CAN 0x412 byte 0 as raw 0-255 = 0-100%. Stock values are flat (20) in every gear.

table.description: Mode 1 of 2 (selected by an internal mode flag, not gear). table.name: CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve
CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve (CAN 0x511 byte 4 (from VDC/ABS), raw x1.301)

table.description: X-input is CAN ID 0x511 payload byte 4, scaled by a fixed 333/256 (~x1.301) factor before this lookup. CAN 0x511 originates from the VDC/ABS module (bytes 0-1 are steering wheel angle, byte 6 vehicle G-force); byte 4 is not identified in the community CAN decoding. Stock data is flat (0) — real, editable, currently inert.

table.name: Gear 1 Shift Correction
table.description:
Gear 1 of 5. Signed correction curve against engine speed, selected by a gear-indexed pointer array at 0x117A0. Gear 1 is all zeros (no correction), and the magnitude falls with each higher gear (about -1970 at the top of gear 2 down to -390 in gear 5) — the shape of a shift-shock or torque-phase correction.
Values are genuinely NEGATIVE and stored as signed 16-bit. Real-world units are not confirmed.
This family was only found after correcting the Ghidra M32R processor definition: the pointer array that selects it was unreadable before.

table.name: CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve
CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve (Reference signal breakpoint (raw, pre-scale CAN 0x410 chain value))

table.description: X-input confirmed via decompilation: the same ceiling-clamped CAN ID 0x410-derived reference value already traced in docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md (before its x256 scale-up), NOT gear-indexed — a single standalone curve. Stock data is a genuine hump shape: rises from 61 to a peak of 127 around the middle of the axis, then falls back to 0 at the high end — a real, currently-populated tunable curve.

table.name: Signal FE Response Curve
Signal FE Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, source not fully traced))

table.description: X-input is an internal RAM value (traced back through several conditional assignments in the decompiled code, but not yet to a specific sensor or CAN ID — see docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Stock data is a real, populated step curve (64 up to 256), not flat/placeholder.

table.name: Smoothed Signal Response Curve
Smoothed Signal Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, x256 of a 0-255 byte))

table.description: X-input is the same internal signal as the 'Signal FE Response Curve' table, but smoothed through a calibratable first-order filter before this lookup (confirmed via decompilation: the filter target is that byte shifted left 8, i.e. x256). This is a DIFFERENT signal chain from the engine-speed tables, so the RPM scale used on those does NOT apply here — left raw deliberately. Stock data is a real, populated rising curve (200 up to 1189).

table.name: Shift Map - ATFTempLow, 1
table.description:
THE SHIFT MAP. All eight shift points in one table, in the form a five-speed automatic is normally calibrated: vehicle speed against accelerator pedal angle, one row per shift event.
Read a cell as: this shift happens at this road speed when the pedal is at this position. Raise a value to delay the shift, lower it to bring the shift on earlier. The upshift rows come first, then the downshifts - the gap between an upshift and its matching downshift is the hysteresis that stops the transmission hunting between two gears, so move the pair together unless you specifically intend to change it.
Every value is vehicle speed in km/h, confirmed against the factory shift chart. The axis is accelerator opening angle, stored as 0-255 for 0-100%.
Cells showing '-' are not editable. They are pedal positions where that particular curve has no vertex in the ROM, so there is no byte to change. Each curve is stored as its own polyline with its own breakpoints; this table lines them up on the shared pedal axis and leaves a gap where a curve does not use a position, rather than inventing a value.
Requires the patched RomRaider in romraider-5eat/. The eight curves sit at eight separate addresses with different lengths, which upstream cannot express as one table - see Table3D.cellIndices.
The schedule used in ATFTempLow drive mode with the lever in Manual 1.
The firmware picks a schedule by index:
drive mode x 50 + shift lever x 10 + gear x 2
Drive modes are Normal, Sport#, Slope, Manual, Kickdown, ATF Temp Low, I-Mode and three not yet identified. Lever positions are D and Manual 5 together, then Manual 4, 3, 2 and 1.
Schedules share curves - a table used in D is often the same object used in Manual 5 - so editing one map can change another. Check the addresses if that matters.
The formula, the drive mode mapping and this naming are rimwall's, from the RomRaider forum thread; FINDINGS section 51 verifies them against the code.

Read a cell as: this shift happens at this road speed when the pedal is at this position. Raise a value to delay the shift, lower it to bring the shift on earlier. The upshift rows come first, then the downshifts - the gap between an upshift and its matching downshift is the hysteresis that stops the transmission hunting between two gears, so move the pair together unless you specifically intend to change it.
Every value is vehicle speed in km/h, confirmed against the factory shift chart. The axis is accelerator opening angle, stored as 0-255 for 0-100%.
Cells showing '-' are not editable. They are pedal positions where that particular curve has no vertex in the ROM, so there is no byte to change. Each curve is stored as its own polyline with its own breakpoints; this table lines them up on the shared pedal axis and leaves a gap where a curve does not use a position, rather than inventing a value.
Requires the patched RomRaider in romraider-5eat/. The eight curves sit at eight separate addresses with different lengths, which upstream cannot express as one table - see Table3D.cellIndices.
The schedule used in Slope drive mode with the lever in Manual 3.
The firmware picks a schedule by index:
drive mode x 50 + shift lever x 10 + gear x 2
Drive modes are Normal, Sport#, Slope, Manual, Kickdown, ATF Temp Low, I-Mode and three not yet identified. Lever positions are D and Manual 5 together, then Manual 4, 3, 2 and 1.
Schedules share curves - a table used in D is often the same object used in Manual 5 - so editing one map can change another. Check the addresses if that matters.
The formula, the drive mode mapping and this naming are rimwall's, from the RomRaider forum thread; FINDINGS section 51 verifies them against the code.

table.name: Downshift 2-1 Pressure - km/h
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE TARGET, 2-1. The pressure commanded during this particular downshift, against vehicle speed.
Pressure is in kPa on the scale confirmed against the factory manual - these maps reach 1372 kPa, which is the manual's figure for full throttle in D.
Raising a value makes this downshift firmer and faster; lowering it makes it softer and slower, at the cost of more clutch slip during the change. Pair it with the ramp step and duration tables in this category, which control how quickly the pressure is allowed to get there.
This table holds ONE of the two quantities in the record array, so it can be shown in real units. Rows are the polyline vertices in order: 1a is the start of segment 1, 1b its end, 2a the start of segment 2, and so on. A segment's end normally equals the next segment's start; where it does not, the curve steps vertically at that point, which is deliberate. The companion table in the same category holds the other quantity, row for row.

A segment's end normally equals the next segment's start; where it does not, the curve steps vertically at that point, which is deliberate. The companion table in the same category holds the other quantity, row for row.

table.name: Downshift 5-3 Pressure - kPa
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE TARGET, 5-3. The pressure commanded during this particular downshift, against vehicle speed.
Pressure is in kPa on the scale confirmed against the factory manual - these maps reach 1372 kPa, which is the manual's figure for full throttle in D.
Raising a value makes this downshift firmer and faster; lowering it makes it softer and slower, at the cost of more clutch slip during the change. Pair it with the ramp step and duration tables in this category, which control how quickly the pressure is allowed to get there.

table.name: Downshift Ramp Step
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE RAMP STEP, one entry per downshift in the order 2-1, 3-1, 3-2, 4-1, 4-2, 4-3, 5-1, 5-2, 5-3, 5-4.
Once the hold period expires, the commanded pressure moves from where it started toward the target by this much. A large value - 32767 appears in the stock calibration for most entries - means effectively no limit, so the pressure goes straight to target. A small value makes the application gradual, which is what the factory calls smooth control.
This is the knob for downshift harshness. Smaller steps are softer and slower.

table.name: Downshift Ramp Hold
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE HOLD DURATION, one entry per downshift in the order 2-1, 3-1, 3-2, 4-1, 4-2, 4-3, 5-1, 5-2, 5-3, 5-4.
How long the pressure is held at its floor before the ramp starts. The value is a count of controller loops. The loop period has NOT been established, so this is left as a raw count rather than converted to milliseconds - a time unit derived from a guessed task rate would look authoritative and be wrong.
Larger values delay the pressure rise, which softens the initial engagement.

table.name: Line Pressure Target 1 - Nm
table.description:
LINE PRESSURE TARGET. Engine torque in, commanded line pressure out. This is what the pressure control solenoid is driven to achieve.
The torque axis is the engine torque the ECU reports on CAN 0x412, after the TCU has multiplied it by the Torque Converter Slip Pressure Factor, smoothed it, and multiplied it again by the ATF temperature factor. So the axis is effective torque, not raw crank torque.
Both units are confirmed against outside sources rather than inferred. The torque axis comes from the community CAN decoding of 0x412 bytes 3-4. The pressure axis reproduces the two figures in the factory manual's line pressure test: about 524 kPa at low torque against a specified 490 nominal (385-555 band), and 1372 kPa at 400 Nm against a specified 1370 at full throttle in D.
RAISING THESE RAISES CLAMPING FORCE. Firmer, faster shifts and more clutch holding capacity, at the cost of harsher engagement, more pump load and more heat. Several maps exist and the TCU selects between them by operating state - which state picks which map has NOT been established, so change them as a set unless you have logged which one is active.

A segment's end normally equals the next segment's start; where it does not, the curve steps vertically at that point, which is deliberate. Several maps exist and the TCU selects between them by operating state - which state picks which map has NOT been established, so change them as a set unless you have logged which one is active.
This table holds ONE of the two quantities in the record array, so it can be shown in real units. Rows are the polyline vertices in order: 1a is the start of segment 1, 1b its end, 2a the start of segment 2, and so on. A segment's end normally equals the next segment's start; where it does not, the curve steps vertically at that point, which is deliberate. The companion table in the same category holds the other quantity, row for row.

table.name: P0705
table.description:
P0705 - enable or disable this diagnostic trouble code.
DISABLED writes zero to this code's slot, which makes it identical to the 43 slots the factory already leaves empty. The fault bit still sets internally, but no code number is attached to it, so nothing is reported.
Know what that does and does not do. It suppresses the CODE, not the FAULT - whatever limp-home, pressure or shift behaviour the TCU applies when that bit sets will still happen. You have only stopped it telling you why. Useful after a hardware change that leaves a sensor permanently faulted; a poor idea as a way of silencing a fault you have not diagnosed.
This behaviour is inferred from the table layout, not tested on a vehicle. Zero is what the firmware's own unused slots contain, which is the best evidence available, but nobody has confirmed how a scan tool reports it.
Stored at 0x01DE68 as 0x0705. The code is the P-number in hex, so this reads as P0705.

DISABLED writes zero to this code's slot, which makes it identical to the 43 slots the factory already leaves empty. The fault bit still sets internally, but no code number is attached to it, so nothing is reported.
Know what that does and does not do. It suppresses the CODE, not the FAULT - whatever limp-home, pressure or shift behaviour the TCU applies when that bit sets will still happen. You have only stopped it telling you why. Useful after a hardware change that leaves a sensor permanently faulted; a poor idea as a way of silencing a fault you have not diagnosed.
This behaviour is inferred from the table layout, not tested on a vehicle. Zero is what the firmware's own unused slots contain, which is the best evidence available, but nobody has confirmed how a scan tool reports it.
Stored at 0x01DF12 as 0x0957. The code is the P-number in hex, so this reads as P0957.

table.name: Line Pressure Target 1 (1370 kPa) - RPM
table.description:
Line pressure target against engine speed. Both columns are in real units and neither is inferred: the breakpoint column uses the same /8 engine-speed scaling confirmed elsewhere in this definition, and the value column is already in kPa.
The kPa unit is confirmed against the factory service manual line pressure test (5AT-35), which has the TCU reporting 'P/L Solenoid Target Pressure' to the Subaru Select Monitor in kPa and specifies 1370 kPa at full throttle in D and R. That value appears verbatim in this table in all eleven firmwares, at an address that relocates between them - so it is calibration data, not a coincidence.
WHAT IS NOT CONFIRMED: which hydraulic circuit each of the two curves governs. The value is flat across engine speed within each curve (1370 kPa in one, 953 kPa in the other), and the consuming function has not been traced. The tables are named for what they demonstrably contain rather than for a circuit that would be a guess.
The final breakpoint is 8160 RPM (65280 raw), a max sentinel rather than a real operating point. Raising line pressure increases clamping force and shift firmness; it also increases pump load and wear.
RPM RANGE: engine speed is a uint16 scaled by 1/8, so the highest value these tables can hold is 8191 RPM. The stock calibration already uses breakpoints as high as 8160 RPM elsewhere, so there is room to raise shift and slip breakpoints for a built engine - but a target above 8191 RPM cannot be represented here, and entering one will clip.

table.name: Read This First
table.description:
Firmware: ADE0236000 (cal ID MB562EH, Unknown, 512kb)
Subaru 5EAT TCU (5-speed automatic transmission control unit), Mitsubishi/Renesas M32R CPU.
Firmware: 91D1206000 (MB431M / R9H)
Origin: JDM TCU, MCU wa12212953www (M32R, 144-pin, 384KB). Most likely a 2003-2004 JDM Legacy — the market is stated by the person who dumped it, but the exact year/model is NOT confirmed (the unit had no housing or part-number label). Note this is NOT the 05-06 USDM TCU, which uses a different MCU.
Confirmed: table addresses, DTC list, checksum, gear ratios (raw/1024), Confirmed conversions: gear ratios (raw/1024), engine speed (raw/8), temperature (raw-40 degC), vehicle speed (km/h), accelerator pedal angle (raw/255 = 0-100%). Anything left as "raw" has no confirmed conversion. Pressure units are NOT confirmed and are not stored in the ROM. See docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md for detail.
REQUIRES RomRaider 1.0.0 or later. The shift schedule and record curves are 3D tables; RomRaider 0.8.2 reports "There was an error loading table" for them.
This is a static file editor only — cannot connect live to the vehicle through RomRaider. Run tools/checksum.py after any edit, before flashing.

table.name: Shift Schedule Group Selector
table.description:
SHIFT SCHEDULE GROUP SELECTOR. The transmission carries ten complete shift schedules in each of five groups, and this table decides which GROUP is in use.
Each cell holds a selector code, not a number to scale: 0x81, 0x82, 0x83, 0x85 select schedule groups 2, 3, 4 and 1 0x80, 0x84, 0x8C select group 0 0xFF no override - the current position stands 0x00 entry unused
The firmware reads it as base + index*4 + a sub-index of -3 to +4, so the rows and columns here are the raw storage rather than two named axes; what indexes it is not established.
Worth knowing before changing anything: three firmwares - ACD1207000, ACD1A06000 and ADE0236000 - carry 0x83 where the other thirteen carry 0xFF. Those images force a gear limit where the rest leave the selector alone, so this table really does differ between calibrations and is not boilerplate.
Codes confirmed from the firmware's own comparison chain, which tests exactly 0x80 to 0x85 and 0x8C.

table.name: ATF Blend Window
table.description:
ATF TEMPERATURE BLEND WINDOW. Below the first temperature the transmission uses its cold calibration for solenoid target pressure; above the second it uses the warm one; between them it interpolates linearly between the two.
This is not per-gear or per-solenoid - all seven solenoid channels read the same pair, so widening or narrowing the window changes when every clutch and brake hands over from cold to warm behaviour.
Stock is 15 C to 135 C in every firmware examined. Raising the lower figure keeps cold-ATF pressures in use for longer; lowering the upper figure reaches full warm behaviour sooner.
Confirmed by following all seven solenoid drivers in the decompiled firmware, which interpolate on exactly these two bytes against the ATF reading.

table.name: Gear 1 Slip Comp Pressure B
Gear 1 Slip Comp Pressure B (Accelerator pedal angle x256 minus reference speed (raw))

table.description: Gear 1 of 5. Pressure/duty correction curve. The X-input is (accelerator pedal angle x 256) minus the Reference Speed Baseline lookup — a difference, so the axis itself is raw even though both operands are now identified. Pedal angle arrives on CAN 0x412 byte 0 as raw 0-255 = 0-100%. Stock values are flat (20) in every gear.

CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve (CAN 0x511 byte 4 (from VDC/ABS), raw x1.301)

table.description: X-input is CAN ID 0x511 payload byte 4, scaled by a fixed 333/256 (~x1.301) factor before this lookup. Stock data is flat (0) — real, editable, currently inert.

table.name: Gear 1 Shift Correction
table.description:
Gear 1 of 5. Signed correction curve against engine speed, selected by a gear-indexed pointer array at 0x117A0. Gear 1 is all zeros (no correction), and the magnitude falls with each higher gear (about -1970 at the top of gear 2 down to -390 in gear 5) — the shape of a shift-shock or torque-phase correction.
Values are genuinely NEGATIVE and stored as signed 16-bit. Real-world units are not confirmed.
This family was only found after correcting the Ghidra M32R processor definition: the pointer array that selects it was unreadable before.

table.name: CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve
CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve (Reference signal breakpoint (raw, pre-scale CAN 0x410 chain value))

table.description: X-input confirmed via decompilation: the same ceiling-clamped CAN ID 0x410-derived reference value already traced in docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md (before its x256 scale-up), NOT gear-indexed — a single standalone curve. Stock data is a genuine hump shape: rises from 61 to a peak of 127 around the middle of the axis, then falls back to 0 at the high end — a real, currently-populated tunable curve.

table.name: Signal FE Response Curve
Signal FE Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, source not fully traced))

table.description: X-input is an internal RAM value (traced back through several conditional assignments in the decompiled code, but not yet to a specific sensor or CAN ID — see docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Stock data is a real, populated step curve (64 up to 256), not flat/placeholder.

table.name: Smoothed Signal Response Curve
Smoothed Signal Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, x256 of a 0-255 byte))

table.description: X-input is the same internal signal as the 'Signal FE Response Curve' table, but smoothed through a calibratable first-order filter before this lookup (confirmed via decompilation: the filter target is that byte shifted left 8, i.e. x256). This is a DIFFERENT signal chain from the engine-speed tables, so the RPM scale used on those does NOT apply here — left raw deliberately. Stock data is a real, populated rising curve (200 up to 1189).

table.name: Shift Map - ATFTempLow, 1
table.description:
THE SHIFT MAP. All eight shift points in one table, in the form a five-speed automatic is normally calibrated: vehicle speed against accelerator pedal angle, one row per shift event.
Read a cell as: this shift happens at this road speed when the pedal is at this position. Raise a value to delay the shift, lower it to bring the shift on earlier. The upshift rows come first, then the downshifts - the gap between an upshift and its matching downshift is the hysteresis that stops the transmission hunting between two gears, so move the pair together unless you specifically intend to change it.
Every value is vehicle speed in km/h, confirmed against the factory shift chart. The axis is accelerator opening angle, stored as 0-255 for 0-100%.
Cells showing '-' are not editable. They are pedal positions where that particular curve has no vertex in the ROM, so there is no byte to change. Each curve is stored as its own polyline with its own breakpoints; this table lines them up on the shared pedal axis and leaves a gap where a curve does not use a position, rather than inventing a value.
Requires the patched RomRaider in romraider-5eat/. The eight curves sit at eight separate addresses with different lengths, which upstream cannot express as one table - see Table3D.cellIndices.
The schedule used in ATFTempLow drive mode with the lever in Manual 1.
The firmware picks a schedule by index:
drive mode x 50 + shift lever x 10 + gear x 2
Drive modes are Normal, Sport#, Slope, Manual, Kickdown, ATF Temp Low, I-Mode and three not yet identified. Lever positions are D and Manual 5 together, then Manual 4, 3, 2 and 1.
Schedules share curves - a table used in D is often the same object used in Manual 5 - so editing one map can change another. Check the addresses if that matters.
The formula, the drive mode mapping and this naming are rimwall's, from the RomRaider forum thread; FINDINGS section 51 verifies them against the code.

Read a cell as: this shift happens at this road speed when the pedal is at this position. Raise a value to delay the shift, lower it to bring the shift on earlier. The upshift rows come first, then the downshifts - the gap between an upshift and its matching downshift is the hysteresis that stops the transmission hunting between two gears, so move the pair together unless you specifically intend to change it.
Every value is vehicle speed in km/h, confirmed against the factory shift chart. The axis is accelerator opening angle, stored as 0-255 for 0-100%.
Cells showing '-' are not editable. They are pedal positions where that particular curve has no vertex in the ROM, so there is no byte to change. Each curve is stored as its own polyline with its own breakpoints; this table lines them up on the shared pedal axis and leaves a gap where a curve does not use a position, rather than inventing a value.
Requires the patched RomRaider in romraider-5eat/. The eight curves sit at eight separate addresses with different lengths, which upstream cannot express as one table - see Table3D.cellIndices.
The schedule used in Mode3 drive mode with the lever in Manual 4.
The firmware picks a schedule by index:
drive mode x 50 + shift lever x 10 + gear x 2
Drive modes are Normal, Sport#, Slope, Manual, Kickdown, ATF Temp Low, I-Mode and three not yet identified. Lever positions are D and Manual 5 together, then Manual 4, 3, 2 and 1.
Schedules share curves - a table used in D is often the same object used in Manual 5 - so editing one map can change another. Check the addresses if that matters.
The formula, the drive mode mapping and this naming are rimwall's, from the RomRaider forum thread; FINDINGS section 51 verifies them against the code.

table.name: Shift Map - Sport#, 1
table.description:
THE SHIFT MAP. All eight shift points in one table, in the form a five-speed automatic is normally calibrated: vehicle speed against accelerator pedal angle, one row per shift event.
Read a cell as: this shift happens at this road speed when the pedal is at this position. Raise a value to delay the shift, lower it to bring the shift on earlier. The upshift rows come first, then the downshifts - the gap between an upshift and its matching downshift is the hysteresis that stops the transmission hunting between two gears, so move the pair together unless you specifically intend to change it.
Every value is vehicle speed in km/h, confirmed against the factory shift chart. The axis is accelerator opening angle, stored as 0-255 for 0-100%.
Cells showing '-' are not editable. They are pedal positions where that particular curve has no vertex in the ROM, so there is no byte to change. Each curve is stored as its own polyline with its own breakpoints; this table lines them up on the shared pedal axis and leaves a gap where a curve does not use a position, rather than inventing a value.
Requires the patched RomRaider in romraider-5eat/. The eight curves sit at eight separate addresses with different lengths, which upstream cannot express as one table - see Table3D.cellIndices.
The schedule used in Sport# drive mode with the lever in Manual 1.
The firmware picks a schedule by index:
drive mode x 50 + shift lever x 10 + gear x 2
Drive modes are Normal, Sport#, Slope, Manual, Kickdown, ATF Temp Low, I-Mode and three not yet identified. Lever positions are D and Manual 5 together, then Manual 4, 3, 2 and 1.
Schedules share curves - a table used in D is often the same object used in Manual 5 - so editing one map can change another. Check the addresses if that matters.
The formula, the drive mode mapping and this naming are rimwall's, from the RomRaider forum thread; FINDINGS section 51 verifies them against the code.

table.name: Downshift 2-1 Pressure - km/h
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE TARGET, 2-1. The pressure commanded during this particular downshift, against vehicle speed.
Pressure is in kPa on the scale confirmed against the factory manual - these maps reach 1372 kPa, which is the manual's figure for full throttle in D.
Raising a value makes this downshift firmer and faster; lowering it makes it softer and slower, at the cost of more clutch slip during the change. Pair it with the ramp step and duration tables in this category, which control how quickly the pressure is allowed to get there.
This table holds ONE of the two quantities in the record array, so it can be shown in real units. Rows are the polyline vertices in order: 1a is the start of segment 1, 1b its end, 2a the start of segment 2, and so on. A segment's end normally equals the next segment's start; where it does not, the curve steps vertically at that point, which is deliberate. The companion table in the same category holds the other quantity, row for row.

table.name: Downshift Ramp Step
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE RAMP STEP, one entry per downshift in the order 2-1, 3-1, 3-2, 4-1, 4-2, 4-3, 5-1, 5-2, 5-3, 5-4.
Once the hold period expires, the commanded pressure moves from where it started toward the target by this much. A large value - 32767 appears in the stock calibration for most entries - means effectively no limit, so the pressure goes straight to target. A small value makes the application gradual, which is what the factory calls smooth control.
This is the knob for downshift harshness. Smaller steps are softer and slower.

table.name: Downshift Ramp Hold
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE HOLD DURATION, one entry per downshift in the order 2-1, 3-1, 3-2, 4-1, 4-2, 4-3, 5-1, 5-2, 5-3, 5-4.
How long the pressure is held at its floor before the ramp starts. The value is a count of controller loops. The loop period has NOT been established, so this is left as a raw count rather than converted to milliseconds - a time unit derived from a guessed task rate would look authoritative and be wrong.
Larger values delay the pressure rise, which softens the initial engagement.

table.name: Line Pressure Target 1 - Nm
table.description:
LINE PRESSURE TARGET. Engine torque in, commanded line pressure out. This is what the pressure control solenoid is driven to achieve.
The torque axis is the engine torque the ECU reports on CAN 0x412, after the TCU has multiplied it by the Torque Converter Slip Pressure Factor, smoothed it, and multiplied it again by the ATF temperature factor. So the axis is effective torque, not raw crank torque.
Both units are confirmed against outside sources rather than inferred. The torque axis comes from the community CAN decoding of 0x412 bytes 3-4. The pressure axis reproduces the two figures in the factory manual's line pressure test: about 524 kPa at low torque against a specified 490 nominal (385-555 band), and 1372 kPa at 400 Nm against a specified 1370 at full throttle in D.

table.name: P0705
table.description:
P0705 - enable or disable this diagnostic trouble code.
DISABLED writes zero to this code's slot, which makes it identical to the 43 slots the factory already leaves empty. The fault bit still sets internally, but no code number is attached to it, so nothing is reported.
Know what that does and does not do. It suppresses the CODE, not the FAULT - whatever limp-home, pressure or shift behaviour the TCU applies when that bit sets will still happen. You have only stopped it telling you why. Useful after a hardware change that leaves a sensor permanently faulted; a poor idea as a way of silencing a fault you have not diagnosed.
This behaviour is inferred from the table layout, not tested on a vehicle. Zero is what the firmware's own unused slots contain, which is the best evidence available, but nobody has confirmed how a scan tool reports it.
Stored at 0x01DC1C as 0x0705. The code is the P-number in hex, so this reads as P0705.

table.name: Line Pressure Target 1 (1370 kPa) - RPM
table.description:
Line pressure target against engine speed. Both columns are in real units and neither is inferred: the breakpoint column uses the same /8 engine-speed scaling confirmed elsewhere in this definition, and the value column is already in kPa.
The kPa unit is confirmed against the factory service manual line pressure test (5AT-35), which has the TCU reporting 'P/L Solenoid Target Pressure' to the Subaru Select Monitor in kPa and specifies 1370 kPa at full throttle in D and R. That value appears verbatim in this table in all eleven firmwares, at an address that relocates between them - so it is calibration data, not a coincidence.
WHAT IS NOT CONFIRMED: which hydraulic circuit each of the two curves governs. The value is flat across engine speed within each curve (1370 kPa in one, 953 kPa in the other), and the consuming function has not been traced. The tables are named for what they demonstrably contain rather than for a circuit that would be a guess.
The final breakpoint is 8160 RPM (65280 raw), a max sentinel rather than a real operating point. Raising line pressure increases clamping force and shift firmness; it also increases pump load and wear.
RPM RANGE: engine speed is a uint16 scaled by 1/8, so the highest value these tables can hold is 8191 RPM. The stock calibration already uses breakpoints as high as 8160 RPM elsewhere, so there is room to raise shift and slip breakpoints for a built engine - but a target above 8191 RPM cannot be represented here, and entering one will clip.

table.name: Read This First
table.description:
Firmware: ACD1A06000 (cal ID MB558D20, JDM, 512kb)
Subaru 5EAT TCU (5-speed automatic transmission control unit), Mitsubishi/Renesas M32R CPU.
Firmware: 91D1206000 (MB431M / R9H)
Origin: JDM TCU, MCU wa12212953www (M32R, 144-pin, 384KB). Most likely a 2003-2004 JDM Legacy — the market is stated by the person who dumped it, but the exact year/model is NOT confirmed (the unit had no housing or part-number label). Note this is NOT the 05-06 USDM TCU, which uses a different MCU.
Confirmed: table addresses, DTC list, checksum, gear ratios (raw/1024), Confirmed conversions: gear ratios (raw/1024), engine speed (raw/8), temperature (raw-40 degC), vehicle speed (km/h), accelerator pedal angle (raw/255 = 0-100%). Anything left as "raw" has no confirmed conversion. Pressure units are NOT confirmed and are not stored in the ROM. See docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md for detail.
REQUIRES RomRaider 1.0.0 or later. The shift schedule and record curves are 3D tables; RomRaider 0.8.2 reports "There was an error loading table" for them.
This is a static file editor only — cannot connect live to the vehicle through RomRaider. Run tools/checksum.py after any edit, before flashing.

table.name: Shift Schedule Group Selector
table.description:
SHIFT SCHEDULE GROUP SELECTOR. The transmission carries ten complete shift schedules in each of five groups, and this table decides which GROUP is in use.
Each cell holds a selector code, not a number to scale: 0x81, 0x82, 0x83, 0x85 select schedule groups 2, 3, 4 and 1 0x80, 0x84, 0x8C select group 0 0xFF no override - the current position stands 0x00 entry unused
The firmware reads it as base + index*4 + a sub-index of -3 to +4, so the rows and columns here are the raw storage rather than two named axes; what indexes it is not established.
Worth knowing before changing anything: three firmwares - ACD1207000, ACD1A06000 and ADE0236000 - carry 0x83 where the other thirteen carry 0xFF. Those images force a gear limit where the rest leave the selector alone, so this table really does differ between calibrations and is not boilerplate.
Codes confirmed from the firmware's own comparison chain, which tests exactly 0x80 to 0x85 and 0x8C.

table.name: ATF Blend Window
table.description:
ATF TEMPERATURE BLEND WINDOW. Below the first temperature the transmission uses its cold calibration for solenoid target pressure; above the second it uses the warm one; between them it interpolates linearly between the two.
This is not per-gear or per-solenoid - all seven solenoid channels read the same pair, so widening or narrowing the window changes when every clutch and brake hands over from cold to warm behaviour.
Stock is 15 C to 135 C in every firmware examined. Raising the lower figure keeps cold-ATF pressures in use for longer; lowering the upper figure reaches full warm behaviour sooner.
Confirmed by following all seven solenoid drivers in the decompiled firmware, which interpolate on exactly these two bytes against the ATF reading.

table.name: Mode 2 Pressure Threshold E
Mode 2 Pressure Threshold E (Accelerator pedal angle x256 minus reference speed (raw))

table.description: Mode 2 of 2 (selected by an internal mode flag, not gear). Same slip-amount X-formula as Pressure Control B/C/D (confirmed via decompilation: X = smoothed reference * 256 - Reference Speed Baseline lookup). Stock data is flat (0) in both modes — a real, editable table even though it isn't currently varying.

table.name: CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve
CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve (CAN 0x511 byte 4 (from VDC/ABS), raw x1.301)

table.description: X-input is CAN ID 0x511 payload byte 4, scaled by a fixed 333/256 (~x1.301) factor before this lookup. CAN 0x511 originates from the VDC/ABS module (bytes 0-1 are steering wheel angle, byte 6 vehicle G-force); byte 4 is not identified in the community CAN decoding. Stock data is flat (0) — real, editable, currently inert.

table.name: Gear 1 Shift Correction
table.description:
Gear 1 of 5. Signed correction curve against engine speed, selected by a gear-indexed pointer array at 0x117A0. Gear 1 is all zeros (no correction), and the magnitude falls with each higher gear (about -1970 at the top of gear 2 down to -390 in gear 5) — the shape of a shift-shock or torque-phase correction.
Values are genuinely NEGATIVE and stored as signed 16-bit. Real-world units are not confirmed.
This family was only found after correcting the Ghidra M32R processor definition: the pointer array that selects it was unreadable before.

table.name: CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve
CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve (Reference signal breakpoint (raw, pre-scale CAN 0x410 chain value))

table.description: X-input confirmed via decompilation: the same ceiling-clamped CAN ID 0x410-derived reference value already traced in docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md (before its x256 scale-up), NOT gear-indexed — a single standalone curve. Stock data is a genuine hump shape: rises from 61 to a peak of 127 around the middle of the axis, then falls back to 0 at the high end — a real, currently-populated tunable curve.

table.name: Signal FE Response Curve
Signal FE Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, source not fully traced))

table.description: X-input is an internal RAM value (traced back through several conditional assignments in the decompiled code, but not yet to a specific sensor or CAN ID — see docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Stock data is a real, populated step curve (64 up to 256), not flat/placeholder.

table.name: Smoothed Signal Response Curve
Smoothed Signal Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, x256 of a 0-255 byte))

table.description: X-input is the same internal signal as the 'Signal FE Response Curve' table, but smoothed through a calibratable first-order filter before this lookup (confirmed via decompilation: the filter target is that byte shifted left 8, i.e. x256). This is a DIFFERENT signal chain from the engine-speed tables, so the RPM scale used on those does NOT apply here — left raw deliberately. Stock data is a real, populated rising curve (200 up to 1189).

table.name: Shift Map - ATFTempLow, 1
table.description:
THE SHIFT MAP. All eight shift points in one table, in the form a five-speed automatic is normally calibrated: vehicle speed against accelerator pedal angle, one row per shift event.
Read a cell as: this shift happens at this road speed when the pedal is at this position. Raise a value to delay the shift, lower it to bring the shift on earlier. The upshift rows come first, then the downshifts - the gap between an upshift and its matching downshift is the hysteresis that stops the transmission hunting between two gears, so move the pair together unless you specifically intend to change it.
Every value is vehicle speed in km/h, confirmed against the factory shift chart. The axis is accelerator opening angle, stored as 0-255 for 0-100%.
Cells showing '-' are not editable. They are pedal positions where that particular curve has no vertex in the ROM, so there is no byte to change. Each curve is stored as its own polyline with its own breakpoints; this table lines them up on the shared pedal axis and leaves a gap where a curve does not use a position, rather than inventing a value.
Requires the patched RomRaider in romraider-5eat/. The eight curves sit at eight separate addresses with different lengths, which upstream cannot express as one table - see Table3D.cellIndices.
The schedule used in ATFTempLow drive mode with the lever in Manual 1.
The firmware picks a schedule by index:
drive mode x 50 + shift lever x 10 + gear x 2
Drive modes are Normal, Sport#, Slope, Manual, Kickdown, ATF Temp Low, I-Mode and three not yet identified. Lever positions are D and Manual 5 together, then Manual 4, 3, 2 and 1.
Schedules share curves - a table used in D is often the same object used in Manual 5 - so editing one map can change another. Check the addresses if that matters.
The formula, the drive mode mapping and this naming are rimwall's, from the RomRaider forum thread; FINDINGS section 51 verifies them against the code.

table.name: Shift Map - Kickdown, D5
table.description:
THE SHIFT MAP. All eight shift points in one table, in the form a five-speed automatic is normally calibrated: vehicle speed against accelerator pedal angle, one row per shift event.
Read a cell as: this shift happens at this road speed when the pedal is at this position. Raise a value to delay the shift, lower it to bring the shift on earlier. The upshift rows come first, then the downshifts - the gap between an upshift and its matching downshift is the hysteresis that stops the transmission hunting between two gears, so move the pair together unless you specifically intend to change it.
Every value is vehicle speed in km/h, confirmed against the factory shift chart. The axis is accelerator opening angle, stored as 0-255 for 0-100%.
Cells showing '-' are not editable. They are pedal positions where that particular curve has no vertex in the ROM, so there is no byte to change. Each curve is stored as its own polyline with its own breakpoints; this table lines them up on the shared pedal axis and leaves a gap where a curve does not use a position, rather than inventing a value.
Requires the patched RomRaider in romraider-5eat/. The eight curves sit at eight separate addresses with different lengths, which upstream cannot express as one table - see Table3D.cellIndices.
The schedule used in Kickdown drive mode with the lever in P, N, D or Manual 5.
The firmware picks a schedule by index:
drive mode x 50 + shift lever x 10 + gear x 2
Drive modes are Normal, Sport#, Slope, Manual, Kickdown, ATF Temp Low, I-Mode and three not yet identified. Lever positions are D and Manual 5 together, then Manual 4, 3, 2 and 1.
Schedules share curves - a table used in D is often the same object used in Manual 5 - so editing one map can change another. Check the addresses if that matters.

table.name: Shift Map - Mode6, 2
table.description:
THE SHIFT MAP. All eight shift points in one table, in the form a five-speed automatic is normally calibrated: vehicle speed against accelerator pedal angle, one row per shift event.
Read a cell as: this shift happens at this road speed when the pedal is at this position. Raise a value to delay the shift, lower it to bring the shift on earlier. The upshift rows come first, then the downshifts - the gap between an upshift and its matching downshift is the hysteresis that stops the transmission hunting between two gears, so move the pair together unless you specifically intend to change it.
Every value is vehicle speed in km/h, confirmed against the factory shift chart. The axis is accelerator opening angle, stored as 0-255 for 0-100%.
Cells showing '-' are not editable. They are pedal positions where that particular curve has no vertex in the ROM, so there is no byte to change. Each curve is stored as its own polyline with its own breakpoints; this table lines them up on the shared pedal axis and leaves a gap where a curve does not use a position, rather than inventing a value.
Requires the patched RomRaider in romraider-5eat/. The eight curves sit at eight separate addresses with different lengths, which upstream cannot express as one table - see Table3D.cellIndices.

The firmware picks a schedule by index:
drive mode x 50 + shift lever x 10 + gear x 2
Drive modes are Normal, Sport#, Slope, Manual, Kickdown, ATF Temp Low, I-Mode and three not yet identified. Lever positions are D and Manual 5 together, then Manual 4, 3, 2 and 1.
Schedules share curves - a table used in D is often the same object used in Manual 5 - so editing one map can change another. Check the addresses if that matters.
The formula, the drive mode mapping and this naming are rimwall's, from the RomRaider forum thread; FINDINGS section 51 verifies them against the code.

table.name: Shift Map - Sport#, 4
table.description:
THE SHIFT MAP. All eight shift points in one table, in the form a five-speed automatic is normally calibrated: vehicle speed against accelerator pedal angle, one row per shift event.
Read a cell as: this shift happens at this road speed when the pedal is at this position. Raise a value to delay the shift, lower it to bring the shift on earlier. The upshift rows come first, then the downshifts - the gap between an upshift and its matching downshift is the hysteresis that stops the transmission hunting between two gears, so move the pair together unless you specifically intend to change it.
Every value is vehicle speed in km/h, confirmed against the factory shift chart. The axis is accelerator opening angle, stored as 0-255 for 0-100%.
Cells showing '-' are not editable. They are pedal positions where that particular curve has no vertex in the ROM, so there is no byte to change. Each curve is stored as its own polyline with its own breakpoints; this table lines them up on the shared pedal axis and leaves a gap where a curve does not use a position, rather than inventing a value.
Requires the patched RomRaider in romraider-5eat/. The eight curves sit at eight separate addresses with different lengths, which upstream cannot express as one table - see Table3D.cellIndices.

Schedules share curves - a table used in D is often the same object used in Manual 5 - so editing one map can change another. Check the addresses if that matters.

table.name: Downshift 2-1 Pressure - km/h
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE TARGET, 2-1. The pressure commanded during this particular downshift, against vehicle speed.
Pressure is in kPa on the scale confirmed against the factory manual - these maps reach 1372 kPa, which is the manual's figure for full throttle in D.
Raising a value makes this downshift firmer and faster; lowering it makes it softer and slower, at the cost of more clutch slip during the change. Pair it with the ramp step and duration tables in this category, which control how quickly the pressure is allowed to get there.
This table holds ONE of the two quantities in the record array, so it can be shown in real units. Rows are the polyline vertices in order: 1a is the start of segment 1, 1b its end, 2a the start of segment 2, and so on. A segment's end normally equals the next segment's start; where it does not, the curve steps vertically at that point, which is deliberate. The companion table in the same category holds the other quantity, row for row.

table.name: Downshift Ramp Step
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE RAMP STEP, one entry per downshift in the order 2-1, 3-1, 3-2, 4-1, 4-2, 4-3, 5-1, 5-2, 5-3, 5-4.
Once the hold period expires, the commanded pressure moves from where it started toward the target by this much. A large value - 32767 appears in the stock calibration for most entries - means effectively no limit, so the pressure goes straight to target. A small value makes the application gradual, which is what the factory calls smooth control.
This is the knob for downshift harshness. Smaller steps are softer and slower.

table.name: Downshift Ramp Hold
table.description:
DOWNSHIFT PRESSURE HOLD DURATION, one entry per downshift in the order 2-1, 3-1, 3-2, 4-1, 4-2, 4-3, 5-1, 5-2, 5-3, 5-4.
How long the pressure is held at its floor before the ramp starts. The value is a count of controller loops. The loop period has NOT been established, so this is left as a raw count rather than converted to milliseconds - a time unit derived from a guessed task rate would look authoritative and be wrong.
Larger values delay the pressure rise, which softens the initial engagement.

table.name: Line Pressure Target 1 - Nm
table.description:
LINE PRESSURE TARGET. Engine torque in, commanded line pressure out. This is what the pressure control solenoid is driven to achieve.
The torque axis is the engine torque the ECU reports on CAN 0x412, after the TCU has multiplied it by the Torque Converter Slip Pressure Factor, smoothed it, and multiplied it again by the ATF temperature factor. So the axis is effective torque, not raw crank torque.
Both units are confirmed against outside sources rather than inferred. The torque axis comes from the community CAN decoding of 0x412 bytes 3-4. The pressure axis reproduces the two figures in the factory manual's line pressure test: about 524 kPa at low torque against a specified 490 nominal (385-555 band), and 1372 kPa at 400 Nm against a specified 1370 at full throttle in D.
RAISING THESE RAISES CLAMPING FORCE. Firmer, faster shifts and more clutch holding capacity, at the cost of harsher engagement, more pump load and more heat. Several maps exist and the TCU selects between them by operating state - which state picks which map has NOT been established, so change them as a set unless you have logged which one is active.
This table holds ONE of the two quantities in the record array, so it can be shown in real units. Rows are the polyline vertices in order: 1a is the start of segment 1, 1b its end, 2a the start of segment 2, and so on. A segment's end normally equals the next segment's start; where it does not, the curve steps vertically at that point, which is deliberate. The companion table in the same category holds the other quantity, row for row.

table.name: P0705
table.description:
P0705 - enable or disable this diagnostic trouble code.
DISABLED writes zero to this code's slot, which makes it identical to the 43 slots the factory already leaves empty. The fault bit still sets internally, but no code number is attached to it, so nothing is reported.
Know what that does and does not do. It suppresses the CODE, not the FAULT - whatever limp-home, pressure or shift behaviour the TCU applies when that bit sets will still happen. You have only stopped it telling you why. Useful after a hardware change that leaves a sensor permanently faulted; a poor idea as a way of silencing a fault you have not diagnosed.
This behaviour is inferred from the table layout, not tested on a vehicle. Zero is what the firmware's own unused slots contain, which is the best evidence available, but nobody has confirmed how a scan tool reports it.
Stored at 0x01DE78 as 0x0705. The code is the P-number in hex, so this reads as P0705.
